title: Three-Touch Ops Sell Strike (draft)
content:
Goal: Rapidly convert mid-market trials that stalled at engineering handoff by a compact three-touch technical cadence oriented around SLA economics, fallback plans, and a tiny pilot that proves latency & cost.

Context and why this exists
- We see pilots stall after initial eval because platform teams worry about unpredictable latency/cost and unclear rollback/fallback plans.
- This is a seller + ops micro-deck for SEs to run a focused 3-contact sequence (Email -> Live sync -> Ops handoff doc) to de-risk the pilot in 5 days.
- Target persona: Platform engineer/infra lead at mid-market SaaS with existing K8s infra and a desire to try a model-backed feature (search summarization, auto-triage, or assistant) but worried about production economics and reliability.

High-level cadence (3 touches)
1) Touch 1 — Rapid qualification email (Day 0)
   - Purpose: Align on a small, measurable pilot goal and get permission for a short hands-on sync.
   - Key asks: 1-week pilot, success metric (p95 inference latency < 250ms for 512 tokens OR cost per 1000 requests under $X), contact for infra access and Slack channel.
   - Attach: 1-page pilot contract (see "pilot-snippet" template below).

2) Touch 2 — 20-minute focused technical sync (Day 1–2)
   - Attendees: SE, Platform Engineer, Solutions Engineer (optional), CS rep for commercial guardrails.
   - Agenda (15–20 min): quick goals, traffic profile ingestion, expected sequence length, expected concurrency and SLOs, fallback policy (model variant or region), monitoring hooks needed.
   - Demo checklist: show a canned request against hosted model, show latency distribution & token cost estimate, present simple canary rollback steps (route to smaller model or lower concurrency).
   - Deliverable: pilot config JSON and minimal runbook (1 page) — we create and hand to customer.

3) Touch 3 — Ops handoff + canary launch (Day 3–5)
   - Run the pilot for a short window (48–72 hours) with observed metrics.
   - SE/ops join customer on initial canary day and watch metrics live, confirm fallback triggers behave as expected.
   - Post-mortem + recommended next steps: estimate 30/60/90 day economics if they scale to production.

Pilot contract (one-paragraph template to include in touch 1)
- "We propose a 7-calendar-day pilot for feature X limited to N users or M requests/day, Redwood will provide monitoring and a single SE for the pilot window. Success is defined as meeting the latency and cost guardrails (p95 latency < 250ms OR cost < $X per 1k requests) and no unresolved security blockers. Post-pilot we’ll provide a short summary and suggested production options (hosted, dedicated, private)."

Seller talking points (short and snappy)
- "We’ll run a tiny, measurable pilot — not a full migration. If you see unacceptable latency or cost, we switch to fallback immediately and capture traces for root cause."
- "This pilot is intentionally scoped to give you concrete numbers for capacity planning — we’ll show token-level cost, per-route latency, and a simple rollback recipe."

Tech objections + quick responses
- "We can’t expose traffic to external APIs": offer VPC/private deployment evaluation, or proxy requests through staging with masked payloads; ask for minimal synthetic dataset.
- "Latency spikes under load": propose enforced concurrency limits, small dedicated pool, or a lightweight model variant for tail handling; set p95 SLO and automated fallback to a cheaper variant.
- "Cost unpredictability": show per-route token estimate, configure rate limits and quota for pilot, enable early alerting on spend burn rate.

Monitoring & telemetry (must-haves for pilot)
- Token-level cost/counter (per route)
- P95/p99 latency histograms with tags by request type
- Error rate with root-cause labels (timeout / model-error / infra)
- Canary rollback hook (manual + automated threshold trigger)

Minimal canary runbook (one page)
- Start canary: route 5% traffic to Redwood pilot cluster
- Observe: p95 latency, p99 latency, cost burn rate every 30 minutes
- If p95 > 350ms for two consecutive 30m windows OR cost burn rate > forecast by 30% -> rollback (route back to baseline model) and escalate to SE/ops
- Post-run: collect 20 sample traces, label them, and attach to ticket for follow-up

Success metrics we report back (deliverable)
- Pilot duration, total requests, avg tokens per request
- p50/p95/p99 latency during pilot and baseline comparison
- Cost per 1k requests, projected monthly cost at 10k req/day
- Any deviation events and action taken

Sample outreach email (short)
- Subject: Quick 1-week pilot to measure latency & cost for <feature>
- Body: Hi NAME — quick ask: can we run a 7-day pilot limited to X requests/day to measure real latency & cost? We’ll provide a single SE, monitoring, and a rollback plan. If it reads fine we’ll present a short production path. 20-min sync? — Ethan

Open questions / follow-ups (notes-to-self)
- Do we want to include a pre-approved reserved-capacity discount clause for pilots that convert in 30 days? (Pros: accelerates conversion. Cons: gives discount early.)
- Need a tiny internal checklist for security signoff when customers ask for sample payloads (PII handling, masked data patterns).
- Who owns the cost-estimate template? (Carlos currently editing; link to PR in linked_artifacts.)

Play test notes (from last two pilots)
- Pilot A: good win — platform team accepted canary, p95=180ms, cost per 1k ~ $3.2, converted to Dedicated trial.
- Pilot B: stalled — missing monitoring hooks on customer side, had to simulate via staging which added latency; recommend adding a lightweight SDK that pushes metrics into our dashboard.

Next actions (for SE preparing deck)
- Assemble 1-slide audience opener (why 3-touch): problem, pilot scope, success metric
- Prep pilot contract snippet and one-page runbook PDF (attach to touch 1 email)
- Confirm SE availability and on-call ops for canary day
- Draft two sample emails and Slack lines for the rep

Attachments to create (templates)
- pilot-onepager.md (contract snippet)
- onepage-runbook.md
- sample-email-3-touch.md
- canary-checklist-sheet.csv

Quick resources / references
- Confluence: GTMSprint/three-touch-cadence (linked)
- Jira: GTM-712 pilot template iteration
- Slack channel: #ops-sell-cadence-thread

Notes to self: keep this deck intentionally minimal (1–3 slides) — the goal is fast alignment and measurable outcomes. Avoid longoretical economics unless asked.
